jobs.description:

Maven Clinic is the world's largest virtual clinic for women and families on a mission to make healthcare work for all of us. Through Maven Enterprise, the company partners with more than 2,300 employers and health plans to provide end-to-end women's and family health programs spanning fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, and menopause and midlife — improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs, and expanding equitable access to high-quality care at scale. Founded in 2014 by CEO Kate Ryder, Maven Clinic has raised more than $425 million from leading healthcare and technology investors including General Catalyst, Sequoia, Dragoneer Investment Group, Oak HC/FT, StepStone Group, Icon Ventures, and Lux Capital. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission –  Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including: 

  • TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)
  • Fortune Change the World (2024)
  • CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)
  • Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the Role: 

As a Senior Executive Assistant, you will support four to five members of Maven’s C-suite and play an important role in helping them use their time effectively. You’ll manage complex calendars, coordinate travel and meetings, anticipate needs, and keep priorities and follow-ups moving. This role calls for strong judgment, discretion, and a calm, proactive approach. You’ll work closely with the executives you support, the broader Executive Assistant team, and partners across Maven to make sure the details are handled and leaders are prepared to focus on the work that matters most.

What you'll do:

  • Manage complex calendars and scheduling. Coordinate internal and external meetings across competing priorities, maintain clean calendars, and proactively resolve conflicts. Build in appropriate preparation, travel, and follow-up time.
  • Help executives make the best use of their time. Learn their priorities and working styles, flag calendar tradeoffs, identify meetings that may need to be delegated or reconsidered, and surface conflicts or risks early.
  • Coordinate meetings from start to finish. Prepare agendas and materials as needed, confirm attendees and logistics, and make sure meeting links, rooms, and technology are ready. Help executives prepare for high-stakes conversations and track resulting follow-ups.
  • Manage travel and expenses. Arrange door-to-door travel and accommodations, share clear itineraries and relevant materials in advance, monitor travel changes, and submit expenses promptly in line with company policy.
  • Communicate on executives’ behalf. Serve as a thoughtful point of contact for colleagues and external stakeholders. Draft and coordinate clear, concise communications that reflect each executive’s tone and priorities.
  • Support board and investor logistics. Coordinate scheduling, materials, and logistics for board meetings, investor interactions, and other external stakeholder engagements, with discretion and care. Place after “Own logistics of events and gatherings.”
  • Track work and close loops. Maintain an organized view of open tasks, deadlines, and commitments; keep executives and stakeholders informed; and make sure handoffs have clear owners and next steps. Be comfortable working cross-functionally with teams that your execs depend on.
  • Support special projects. Take ownership of selected projects that improve executive operations, team coordination, or the EA team’s shared resources. Identify and implement process improvements for your executives and the EA team.
  • Own logistics of events and gatherings. Coordinate executive and team meetings, offsites, dinners, celebrations, and other events, managing logistics and working with internal partners and vendors often on the ground.

About the Customer Digital Experience Team

Customer Digital Experience sits within the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer Success organization.

Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it.

Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to.

We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together.

About the Role

As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change.

It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone.

You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built.

If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on.

jobs.title: Natera: Senior Director, AI Diagnostics
jobs.description:
Headquarters: US Remote

Natera is hiring a Senior Director to lead the research, development and clinical translation of AI and computational algorithms for oncology diagnostics, from research prioritization through validation, deployment, and ongoing performance monitoring. Natera’s longitudinal oncology data resources span tumor genomics, ctDNA, transcriptomics, pathology images, and clinical outcomes, creating opportunities to develop and validate models across molecular, imaging, and clinical data. This role turns that data into multimodal AI products that change how oncologists treat patients. 

We are looking for a scientific leader with a compelling vision for how foundation models can advance oncology diagnostics. You will shape our foundation model strategy - identifying the highest-value opportunities in longitudinal molecular, imaging, and clinical data, defining the capabilities we need to build, and guiding their translation into clinically useful products. This requires both the imagination to pursue new possibilities and the judgment to establish where these approaches deliver meaningful advantages.  You will lead an established algorithm team, develop its technical and leadership capabilities, and recruit talent aligned with the product roadmap. With Product and other partners, you will set strategy and decide which opportunities move toward clinical deployment.

Key Responsibilities:

Build and lead the team: Grow the existing algorithm research team, hire key talent, and set a high bar for scientific rigor and execution.

Own the path from research to launch: Establish development milestones and evidence-based go/no-go criteria from feasibility through validation and launch, with clear ownership, reproducible analyses, and documented decisions.

Set strategy with Product: Partner with Product, Clinical, and Commercial leaders to prioritize clinical use cases, define intended use and success criteria, and make investment, continuation, and stop decisions based on evidence, feasibility, and clinical and business value.

Push the technical frontier: Bring in foundation models and multimodal deep learning, and turn our data into products that set us apart from competitors.

Deliver with quality: Make sure every algorithm is built on clean data, validated rigorously, and monitored after launch, so it holds up for clinicians, patients, and regulators.

Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Machine Learning, Biostatistics, or a related quantitative field. A Master’s degree with substantial additional experience will be considered.
  • Substantial experience developing computational products, including sustained leadership of multidisciplinary teams and ownership of complex development programs through clinical deployment. Demonstrated scope and impact equivalent to a Senior Director are more important than prior title.
  • Demonstrated ability to define and advance a foundation model research strategy, grounded in a deep understanding of representation learning, pretraining, adaptation, and evaluation. Able to articulate an original, clinically grounded vision, translate it into a research roadmap, and guide teams through consequential scientific and technical decisions.
  • Demonstrated accountability for taking at least one AI/ML or computational algorithm from research through validation and clinical deployment within a diagnostic product. Candidates should be able to explain their decisions, validation responsibilities, cross-functional role, and post-launch results.
  • Strong understanding of analytical and clinical validation for regulated diagnostics, including what regulators expect from AI-based products.
  • Depth in at least one oncology data modality, such as NGS, liquid biopsy, transcriptomics, or whole-slide imaging, and sufficient breadth to lead across modalities. Able to challenge model design, data assumptions, evaluation methods, and Python-based analyses through technical reviews; routine coding is not a core responsibility.
  • Demonstrated experience managing people managers and developing technical leaders, building development processes that teams adopt, and influencing senior stakeholders across R&D, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, and Commercial without direct authority.
  • Experience overseeing algorithm deployment and lifecycle management, including reproducible implementation, model and data versioning, release controls, and post-launch performance monitoring, in partnership with Engineering

About the Job:

Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.

As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”

Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.

Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

  • Product & Value
    • Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.
    • Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.

Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.
    • Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.
  • Executive & Growth
    • Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.
    • Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.
  • Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)
    • Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.
  • Delivery & Execution
    • Run the delivery rhythm: status calls and reporting, accountability to tasks and deadlines across the engagement team, and escalation of technical or political blockers.
    • Keep a running view of budget/burn against SOW and flag over/under-pr
